blocks.text: 1. Parametric vs Non-Parametric Memory
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446707209-295341890.png

Hallucinations closed by pointing here. Parametric vs Non-Parametric Memory gives a precise name to an idea already used implicitly throughout this course: the knowledge storage distinction behind RAG.
It names the two kinds of memory this course keeps contrasting.
2. Recapping The Preview
Parametric versus non-parametric memory was previewed in that earlier topic as formalizing the knowledge storage distinction.
This topic works through that distinction in full.
3. Recapping Frozen Weights Knowledge
Every fact a plain model appears to know is encoded somewhere inside its trained weights, the same weights covered across the Deep Learning course.
This style of storage is what gets formally called parametric memory.
4. Parametric Memory Defined
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446707210-124754305.png
Parametric memory means knowledge compressed and encoded directly into a model's numeric parameters.
Nothing external needs to be consulted; the answer is already baked in.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Memory type","Where knowledge lives"],"rows":[["Parametric memory","Compressed inside a model's own numeric weights"],["Non-parametric memory","External, readable documents, searched at query time"]]}

blocks.text: 5. Non-Parametric Memory Defined
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446707211-564981314.png
Non-parametric memory instead keeps knowledge external, stored as actual, readable documents.
Those documents live in vector databases and get searched at query time instead of being baked into weights.
6. RAG As A Hybrid Memory System

blocks.alt: RAG As A Hybrid Memory System
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446707212-327352388.png
RAG combines both kinds of memory together into one working system.
Parametric memory provides language ability, and non-parametric memory provides current facts.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This hybrid framing explains why RAG needs both a capable language model and a well maintained document collection, not either alone.

blocks.text: 7. Recapping Update Comparison
Updating parametric memory requires retraining, the costly process covered in Why RAG Is Needed.
Updating non-parametric memory just means editing or adding a document.
8. Capacity Tradeoffs
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446707472-958371665.png
Parametric memory has a fixed capacity set entirely by a model's size.
Non-parametric memory can grow arbitrarily large simply by adding more documents, an important structural difference between the two.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Memory type","Capacity behavior"],"rows":[["Parametric memory","Fixed capacity, set by the model's own size"],["Non-parametric memory","Can grow arbitrarily by adding more documents"]]}

blocks.text: 9. Interpretability Difference
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446707473-46068153.png
Nobody can point to exactly which weight stores a specific fact inside parametric memory.
A non-parametric document, by contrast, can be opened and read directly, an important transparency difference.
10. Recognizing Which Memory Type Fits A Given Kind Of Knowledge

blocks.alt: Recognizing Which Memory Type Fits A Given Kind Of Knowledge
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446707474-475383106.png
Non-parametric memory suits fast-changing, growing, or private facts.
Parametric memory remains well suited to stable language ability and general reasoning.
11. Worked Example
The example below demonstrates the contrast between a fixed parametric fact and an easily updated non-parametric document.

code.content:
# parametric memory: a stand-in for facts baked into a model's own weights
parametric_knowledge = {"capital of france": "Paris"}  # fixed, requires retraining to change

# non-parametric memory: knowledge kept as external documents
non_parametric_documents = ["The company's current CEO is Jane Doe, appointed in 2025."]

def update_non_parametric_memory(documents, new_fact):
    documents.append(new_fact)
    return documents

print(f"Parametric knowledge (fixed until retraining): {parametric_knowledge}")
print(f"Non-parametric documents before update: {non_parametric_documents}")

non_parametric_documents = update_non_parametric_memory(
    non_parametric_documents, "The company's current CEO is John Smith, appointed in 2026."
)
print(f"Non-parametric documents after a simple update: {non_parametric_documents}")
print("\nNotice: updating non-parametric memory took one line of code; updating parametric memory would require retraining")

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows a new fact added instantly to non-parametric memory, while the parametric dictionary stays completely fixed.

blocks.text: 12. Common Mistakes

items: Confusing which memory type actually requires retraining versus a simple document edit.
Assuming non-parametric memory alone can produce fluent, well-formed language without a capable model.
Treating parametric memory as infinitely expandable rather than fixed by a model's own size.
Overlooking that RAG needs both memory types working together, not either one alone.

blocks.text: 13. Key Takeaways

items: Parametric memory means knowledge compressed directly into a model's own numeric weights.
Non-parametric memory keeps knowledge external, as actual documents searched at query time.
RAG combines both: parametric memory for language ability, non-parametric for current facts.
Updating parametric memory requires costly retraining; updating non-parametric memory means editing documents.
Parametric memory has a fixed capacity set by model size; non-parametric memory can grow arbitrarily.
Parametric memory is opaque, with no way to trace a fact to a specific weight.
Non-parametric documents can be opened and directly, humanly read.
Non-parametric memory suits fast-changing or private facts; parametric memory suits stable language ability.
Next up: RAG Architecture, mapping out the full system built from these two kinds of memory.
